verdict.rationale: npm's own docs say that running `npm install` in a node program installs its dependencies, which is the one-command bootstrap this story asks for. A community comment confirms developers use `npm ci` on branch checkouts, though they find it slow; that is a speed complaint, not a contradiction. missing for 10: in-depth first-party docs that `npm install`/`npm ci` install everything declared in package.json (including dev, optional and workspace dependencies), and documented lockfile-exact reproducibility for a fresh clone.

support.subject: As a developer, I can bootstrap a fresh clone with one command that installs everything the project declares

citations.quote: The very first thing you will most likely want to run in any node program is `npm install` to install its dependencies.
If you create a lock file while using the default registry you can switch to another registry and npm will install packages from the new registry
